title: Recombinant Collagen I Peptide Microcarriers for Cell Expansion and Their Potential Use As Cell Delivery System in a Bioreactor Model
protocol: Remove spongy bone from the femur head using a sterile spoon.
Insert the removed spongy bone into two 50 mL tubes.
Wash the spongy bone with DMEM-F12 (1:1 mixture of DMEM and Ham F12 medium).
Fill each tube with approximately 30 mL of medium.
Shake the tube manually in a longitudinal way for 5 seconds.
Centrifuge the tubes at 300 x g and 22 °C for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the fat-cell layer and approximately 20 mL of the remaining supernatant using a graduated plastic pipette.
Let enough medium remain to cover the spongy bone.
Fill the tubes with 10 ml of DMEM-F12 and shake vigorously longitudinally by hand for 10 - 15 seconds.
Transfer 10 - 15 mL of cell suspension from the tubes to a new 50 mL tube using a graduated plastic pipette.
Repeat steps from aspirating the fat-cell layer until the spongy bone collected in the 50 mL tube is white.
Transfer the cell suspension with a graduated plastic pipette to two new tubes, avoiding aspirating the collagen pellet on the bottom of the 50 mL tubes.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 x g and 22 °C for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant by aspirating it with a graduated plastic pipette.
Add 40 mL of DMEM-F12 supplemented with 10% FCS, 1% Pen/Strep, and 50 µg/mL Ascorbate-2-phosphate to a third tube.
Transfer 5 mL of this medium to each tube containing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellets by flicking the bottom of the tubes vigorously and transfer the cell suspensions to the tube containing only medium.
Dilute 100 µL of cells suspension for cell counting, first diluting with PBS in a ratio of 1:100, then further diluting with trypan blue at a ratio of 1:10.
Add 15 µL of the first dilution to 30 µL DPBS and 15 µL Trypan Blue for counting cells.
Count the cells using a standard Neubauer chamber.
Seed the cells at 109 cells/175 cm2 T-Flask in 25 mL of medium.
Alternatively, divide the whole cell suspension into up to ten 175 cm2 cell culture flasks without counting.
Change the medium after 4 days from seeding.
Perform a complete removal of the culture medium with a graduated plastic pipette for medium exchange.
Wash adherent cells two times with DPBS by adding and removing completely 10 mL of DPBS per flask.
Add 20 mL of fresh medium to each flask.
Treat the skin biopsies and isolate the HDMECs according to previously published protocols.
After separation of dermis from epidermis, incubate the dermis in trypsin for 40 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Transfer the dermis to a Petri dish containing culture medium after incubation time.
Scratch each piece with the use of a scalpel.
Transfer the obtained cell suspension to a 50 mL plastic tube.
Centrifuge the tube for 5 min at 300 x g and 22 °C.
Count the cell suspension using a Neubauer chamber.
Seed the cells at a density of 1.2 x 10^4 cells/cm^2.
Change the medium completely every other day.
Set up spinner flasks one day before experiments.
Prepare spinner flasks for sterilization by autoclave.
Wrap the spinner flasks with aluminum foil around the side caps separately to avoid contamination during unwrapping.
Weigh the required amount of RCP macroporous microcarriers in 20 mL of DPBS (30 mg per spinner flask).
Let the microcarriers hydrate for at least 1 h before heat sterilization by autoclave (121 °C for 15 min).
Use the bioreactor system described to produce vascularized tissue equivalents.
Connect the vessel with the medium reservoir and the pressure bottle through silicon tubes.
Place the connected setup in an autoclave plastic bag, close well, and place it in a second autoclave plastic bag.
Sterilize by autoclaving.
Let RCP macroporous microcarriers settle to the bottom and wash them with 10 mL of culture medium.
Repeat washing RCP macroporous microcarriers three times.
Wash spinner flasks with 10 mL of culture medium.
Add 30 mg of RCP macroporous microcarriers per spinner flask in 8 mL of culture medium.
Equilibrate the spinner flasks containing the RCP microcarriers at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 30 min before seeding cells.
Seed 5 x 10^5 hBMSCs or HDMECs (passage 3) per spinner flask in 2 mL of culture medium.
Place the spinner flasks on the stirrer plate and start stirring at 90 rpm for 5 min.
Rest for 55 min, at 37 °C and 5% CO2, for a total of 1 h static/dynamic incubation.
Repeat static/dynamic incubation four times.
Add 10 mL of cell culture medium per spinner flask.
Start continuous stirring at 95 rpm.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Take samples using a micropipette at days 1, 4, and 7: 333 µL for DNA content (~0.5 mg), 1000 µL for SEM analysis (~1.5 mg), and 333 µL for live/dead staining (~0.5 mg).
Wait until RCP microcarriers settle to the bottom.
Aspirate 10 mL of culture medium from the spinner flask using a 10 mL pipette.
Add 10 mL of fresh culture medium to the spinner flask.
Change the culture medium every other day.
Incubate cultures on the stirrer plate set at 95 rpm, at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 7 days.
Collect approximately 0.5 mg of microcarriers from each spinner flask (in 333 µL suspension) using a micropipette.
Transfer collected microcarriers to a 2 mL plastic tube.
Wash once with 1 mL DPBS, then aspirate the supernatant.
Remove remaining DPBS in a lyophilizer and weight the lyophilized microcarriers for normalization purposes.
Freeze samples at -80 °C for at least 6 hours.
Incubate samples at 60 °C overnight with 300 µL papain 5 U/mL.
Establish the appropriate titration curves according to the manufacturer's instructions of the quantitation assay kit.
Perform measurement of the fluorescent signal at 520 nm using a luminescence detector.
Collect approximately 1 mg of microcarriers from each spinner flask.
Transfer collected microcarriers to a 2 mL plastic tube.
Wash microcarriers once with 1 mL of DPBS.
Remove DPBS and incubate in 1 mL of 70% ethanol for 1 hour.
Remove supernatant and incubate in 1 mL of 80% ethanol for 1 hour.
Remove supernatant and incubate in 1 mL of 90% ethanol for 1 hour.
Remove supernatant and incubate in 1 mL of 100% ethanol for 1 hour.
Remove supernatant and incubate in 1 mL of hexamethyldisilazane for 10 minutes.
Open cap and let the samples dry overnight under a chemical hood.
Fix samples on appropriate support.
Proceed to SEM analysis according to established protocols.
At day 2, 4, and 7 after cell seeding on microcarriers, collect 0.5 mg of microcarriers from each spinner flask.
Transfer collected microcarriers to a 2 mL plastic tube.
Wash once with 1 mL of DPBS.
Fix samples for 10 minutes in enough 4% paraformaldehyde to cover them.
Wash once with 1 mL of DPBS.
Incubate at room temperature with the staining solution for 45 minutes on a rocking shaker.
Detect DAPI fluorescent signal on a fluorescence microscope using a 420 nm emission filter.
Acquire images.
Incubate samples in 500 µL of Live/Dead dye solution.
Keep the samples at 37 °C for 20 min, protected from light.
Wash once with 1 mL of DPBS.
Detect fluorescence signal of living cells with a 490 nm emission filter.
Detect fluorescence signal of dead cells with a 545 nm emission filter on a fluorescence microscope.
Acquire images.
Mix 330 µL of collagen R solution at 0.4% with 170 µL of 0.1% acetic acid and 50 µL of medium M199 in a 15 mL plastic tube.
Keep the mixture on ice.
Take ~0.375 mg of microcarriers (250 µL) using a micropipette.
Transfer the microcarriers to a 1.5 mL plastic tube, wait for RCP microcarriers to settle at the bottom and remove the medium completely.
Determine in advance the volume of NaOH 0.2 N required to neutralize the collagen mixture until it turns from yellow color to pink.
Mix the neutralized collagen mixture immediately with the RCP microcarriers.
Plate the collagen gel-RCP microcarrier mixture in a well of a 24-well plate.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Add 200 µL of vascular endothelial growth factor (e.g., VascuLife VEGF-Mv culture medium).
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Observe under an inverted phase contrast microscope using a 10X magnification objective.
Acquire images.
Cut open BioVaSc longitudinally on the antimesenteric side.
Fix the opened BioVaSc in a polycarbonate frame.
Disinfect the polycarbonate frame by incubating it for 20 min in a sonic bath at 40 kHz.
Incubate the frame three times in ethanol 70% for 25 minutes each time.
Wash the frame three times with DPBS sterile.
Place the biomatrix-frame system in a 100 mm Petri dish and fill it with vascular endothelial growth factor + 1% Pen/Strep.
Incubate the biomatrix overnight at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Inject 10 x 10^7 HDMECs in 1000 µL of culture medium through the preserved vasculature, using a 2 mL syringe.
Inject approximately 700 μL through the arterial inlet and 300 μL through the vein outlet.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 3 hours to allow cell attachment.
Fill the bioreactor system with 350 mL of vascular endothelial growth factor + 1% Pen/Strep.
Place the frame inside the vessel of the bioreactor.
Connect the arterial and venous pedicles to the vessel.
Start perfusion by connecting the bioreactor system to a Peristaltic pump.
Set the pressure at 10 mmHg and amplitude ±1.
Increase the pressure stepwise every hour until reaching 100 mmHg of pressure, amplitude ±20.
Keep the bioreactor system for 7 days under these conditions at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Mix 330 µL of 0.4% collagen R solution, 170 µL of 0.1% acetic acid, and 50 µL of medium M199 in a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Keep the mixture on ice.
Take the RCP microcarriers from the spinner flasks.
Remove the culture medium completely.
Add the volume of NaOH 0.2 N required to neutralize the collagen mixture.
Immediately mix it with the RCP microcarriers.
Add the collagen gel-RCP microcarriers mixture onto the lumen of the biomatrix.
Allow gelation for 30 min.
Change the medium in the bioreactor by removing all the existing medium completely.
Then add 350 mL of fresh, pre-warmed vascular endothelial growth factor + 1% Pen/Strep.
Connect the bioreactor to the Peristaltic pump and set up the pressure at 100 mmHg and amplitude ±20.
Change the medium every 7 days.
Keep the bioreactor in culture for 21 days.
Disconnect the biomatrix from the bioreactor.
Remove it from the polycarbonate frame.
Cut the obtained piece into 6 sections: 2 for MTT, 2 for paraffin embedding/staining, and 2 for SEM analysis.
Place the sections in a Petri dish.
Wash the sections with enough DPBS to cover them.
Discard the DPBS.
Fix the sections in 4% paraformaldehyde overnight.
Prepare the cassettes for paraffin embedding according to standard protocols.
Cut samples of 3 µm from paraffin blocks for H&E staining using a microtome.
Stain rehydrated sections according to standard protocols.
Place the sections in a Petri dish.
Wash the sections with enough DPBS to cover them.
Discard the DPBS.
Fix the sections with 4.75% glutaraldehyde overnight.
Perform dehydration chain with increasing concentrations of ethanol from 50% to 100%.
Cover the sections with hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) for 10 min.
Discard the used HMDS and add fresh HMDS.
Allow the sections to dry overnight under a fume hood.
Prepare the samples for imaging.
Mix the MTT reagent with vascular endothelial growth factor at a concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Incubate the sections in the MTT solution for 90 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Observe the vascular structures and cell-seeded microcarriers macroscopically or under a bright-field microscope to detect metabolically active cells.
Acquire images.
